author.headline: Senior Project Manager | Healthcare Interoperability | FHIR | AI | Digital Health Innovation

comments.text:
Very interesting.
I wonder how different the results would be with a legacy healthcare system that has no FHIR-native API.
In many organizations, especially outside the Epic ecosystem, the hardest problem is not generating FHIR resources. It's understanding what the source data actually means and rebuilding the clinical context that FHIR expects.
Epic starts much closer to the finish line than most healthcare systems.
In oncology systems, for example, workflow states, protocol logic, dose adjustments, and approval processes are often spread across multiple tables and workflows. Mapping them correctly requires much more than identifying field-to-field relationships.

comments.text:
While definitely cool, I frankly do not see how this or anything it would clearly lead to would improve the actual interoperability issues that preposterously continue to exist.

* Labs: Epic has not implemented the simplest of concepts, a row which can be optionally included at the bottom of the table for each column: PERFLAB (performing lab, for example). Because of this, those in charge of mapping components/LOINC, often either just don't map external values at all, or do so selectively, because their best practices concerns about comparing data from different labs.  For easily 90% of components, this worry is irrational and it 100% leads to providers missing data. I've seen it happen no less than 1000 times. Providers expect when they are trending a patients labs with CE and HT setup, that lab data from separate facilities are clearly being mapped and consolidated right? Otherwise why have this?
i have had to explain this to 100 providers, why they are wrong, and no, it's not a bug. It's a feature.

*Partially struct and unstructured data.  "Encounters are the floor at 67%". This right here is funny from a clinically meaningful data persprective because Encounters are where those data live.
Incongruence of priorities.
